Hello all. I wanted to see what supplements and meal plans that people are on here

I use meal plans, because when you say diet, it's assuming you'll quit it eventually. You should be on a meal plan that you can follow for the rest of your life. Also, what kind of supplements do you take to enhance your fitness, weigh loss, muscle growth? Thermogenics, creatine, testosterone, protein?

For me:

Supplements:

  • Thermogenic pills
  • Post/pre-workout
  • Protein (6 different kinds of protein blend)

As for food:

Breakfast:

  • 3 Eggs
  • 1 Cup of plain Oatmeal w/ added strawberries
  • Green Tea

Mid Morning Snack:

  • Greek Yogurt
  • Walnuts
  • Green Tea

Lunch:

  • Salad
  • Broccoli and carrots
  • Salmon or chicken

Afternoon Snack:

  • Apple
  • Unsalted mixed premium nuts (no peanuts)

Dinner:

  • Salad
  • Broccoli and carrots
  • Steak or Chicken or Fish
  • Sometimes I add a cup of rice, quinoa, or potatoes.

Now, I don't always follow this. I'll go out to eat every now and then or have a few drinks with friends, but this is what I try to stick to on most days.
Supplements and Meal Plans of Voaters?

Avoid white flower and dairy. Only eat whole grain once a week as a treat. Eat food that boosts testosterone and removes estrogen. Avoid food that does the opposite. I start the day with a tea mix. Ginger, chamomile and moringa. Add either lemon or lime juice to that. As well as cayenne pepper and apple cider vinegar.

I take chlorella, fish oil, spirulina and multi vitamin caps with the tea. After that I do some yoga and my work out routine. Then at least an hour walk every day. Unless it rains. Fuck rain.
Intermittent fasting with strictly whole foods. For supplements I use yohimbine and occasionally creatine. I'm down to 11-12% body fat with very little effort outside of my norm.

Here's today. I'm on week three of a cut.

Pre-workout: Four eggs, three chicken breasts, two bananas, a handful of spinach, a carrot. Creatine Monohydrate (powder form), a bee pollen capsule, and a multivitamin.

Post-workout: Blended protein shake w/ 2 scoops of whey, 2 cups of whole milk, a tsp or two of raw honey and 2 more bananas. A fish oil capsule.

Lunch at work: Little baggie of green peas that I brought to work. My fat co-workers laugh at me, and if I had feelings like a normal person they would be hurt.

Once I got home: More green peas. About a cup I think?

Total Calories: ~2,250.

Not bad. So why only whey protein? Also, why do you take creatine monohydrate? I take it now because I got a pound of it for free, but I really dislike creatine because of the water gain.

Also, I feel you about weird looks on food. I have this big lunch box I take to school and work every single day. People always laugh how I eat salad and fish for lunch or that I carry around so much stuff. But, they know it works and always say they need to do something like that.

I get a good deal of protein from just regular food already. Iirc I think the chicken I eat is about 120 grams of protein (I don't weigh them, so it varies). The eggs are another 20 g of protein or so, the milk's 16 grams, and there's probably a bit more in more in my fruits and vegetables. I compete in the 198 lb weight class for my powerlifting meets so the whey's really just there to keep me around the 1:1 gram of protein per pound of bodyweight rule when I'm trying to lose weight.

I do have a thing of casein sitting on my shelf, but I rarely use it. I might take a scoop and down it with water if I'm still feeling hungry hours after my workout, but fiber-rich vegetables seem to do the trick for me.

As for other protein supplements--soy, hemp, w/e; I don't bother. The studies seem to go back and forth on them, and it's too much of a headache for me to be resting between my second and third set of squats for the day wondering if why I'm feeling more tired that day is because I'm taking something different, or if it's all in my head. I'm not anti-supplement by any means, but I try to keep it simple when I can.

Creatine Monohydrate's iffy. I take it mostly just because it's cheap, it's recommended by the Starting Strength resources that I first learned my form from, and it doesn't have any documented health downsides. The water weight seems to accumulate pretty evenly throughout my body, and generally I don't really care what my bodyfat is as long as I have somewhat visible abdominal muscle. The biggest downside to it for me is that it forces me to drink a lot more water and use the restroom more times per day, which gets inconvenient at work.

Also, since I explained the other ones already--the bee pollen capsule is for seasonal allergies (it has other benefits too apparently), the fish oil's for recovery and increased protein synthesis, and the multivitamin helps makes up any micronutrient deficits (which I don't really keep track of, but probably exist anyway).

Ah okay. I'm trying to cut down a bit too. I'm about 14.8% body fat and I'm trying to hit the 10-12% range. I'm pretty swole as it is with muscle already and my wife doesn't want me to be any bigger, so I'm not too carrying in building more muscles, nor do I compete in anything anyways. The only downside I hate about muscle is clothes. I need to go up 2-3 sizes in pants and have the waists tailored in because of my ass and legs.
